prompted_for: Equipment line drawing for the Design and engineering service page (svc-design): black-on-white source for the Illustration component mask
composition: rolled-out drawing sheet as a diagonal isometric ground
transparent wireframe skid standing on the sheet, upper centre
scale ruler and mechanical pencil lying bottom right
P&ID schematic printed on the sheet beneath the skid
roll of paper curling at left edge
layout_devices: object rising out of its own drawing (2D plan to 3D skid)
sheet title block lines in the lower-right corner
diagonal paper plane leading the eye from roll to tools
rendering: x-ray / transparent frame showing tanks inside
line_and_texture: finer lines for P&ID symbols on the sheet
ruler tick marks as fine texture
ui_patterns: possible hotspots on schematic vs physical part
motion_implied: P&ID lines draw on, then the skid extrudes up out of the sheet
t2i_keywords: 3D wireframe equipment rising from its own 2D drawing
transparent skid frame showing vessels inside
title block lines in sheet corner
t2i_prompt: Isometric technical line drawing in black ink on pure white: <CONTENT> drawn as a transparent wireframe standing on the large drawing sheet it was designed on. The sheet is rolled out diagonally, its end curled into a roll, a P&ID schematic and a title block printed on it in finer lines. A triangular scale ruler and a mechanical pencil lie beside it. Uniform hairline strokes, no shading, no fill, no colour, no readable text, generous white margin, crisp contours for a single-colour mask.
signature_idea: The equipment stands up out of its own drawing: the plan becomes the skid.
strengths: tells the design service story in one image without words
links 2D documentation to the physical system, which matters to validation buyers
line-only, maskable, consistent with the drawing set
weaknesses: ruler and pencil are a familiar design cliché
transparent frame with inner tanks gets busy at small sizes
illegible schematic squiggles may look fake up close
brand_fit_why: Precise and calm, ties straight into the drawing-sheet language, slightly clichéd props.
